title: McKinney's Cotton Pickers, Dave Wilborn and Detroit musicians
summary: Allen talks about Dave Wilborn of the McKinney's Cotton Pickers, Jones names Detroit players such as Tommy Saunders and multi-instrumentalist Billy Prince.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: J.R. Short, is that his name? Do you remember him? No. The trumpet player was named Blood. This may have been when you were in Philadelphia or something. Yeah. J.R. Short is in Detroit I think playing with the new McKinney's Cotton Pickers. He was a tuba player down here in the early 60s now, I don't know where you were then. That's a lot. Yeah, well, there were so many of those bands. He's with the new McKinney Cotton Pickers, isn't he? Yeah. I'm a friend of Dave Wilborn. Oh yeah? How on earth did you know him? From Manassas of all places. He was up there. Jazz Festival. And we got to be buddies. In case whoever's listening to this, he is the last surviving member of the McKinney Cotton Pickers. He was the singer of the band. And he was trying to get the band down here for the New Orleans Jazz and Heritage Festival. But something like that makes too much sense. So they, you know, I don't know.

In fact I happened to be listening to the band. Yeah. In fact I happened to be listening to the band. He was trying to get the band down here for the New Orleans Jazz and Heritage Festival. But something like that makes too much sense. So they didn't bring it down.

Yeah. In fact I happened to be listening to that band this morning but on the old McKinney Cotton Pickers, not the new ones. And does Wilburn play an instrument now? No. Wilburn sings. He was a banjo player. Was he? Yeah.

They have two units. They're using a small unit and a large unit. Tommy Saunders is playing trumpet with him sometimes. And Tommy's a wonderful player. And there's some awfully good musicians in the Detroit area too, so I imagine that they can put together some very fine bands. Yeah.
The Gabriel Brothers and their father are up there. Different ones, different New Orleans musicians are up around there too.
I guess the best all around multi-instrumentalist I ever met in my life was from Detroit, went to Wayne State University, Billy Prince. What's his name?

He's something else. He's like I said the most unbelievable multi-instrumentalist. You're telling me about him. He was a, his daddy was Grand Prince who wrote a lot of stocks back in the old days. He was a trumpet player with Ben Burnie and all those old-time bands. Yeah there's an awful lot of good players out there. They all have a good symphony orchestra. Yeah.
